A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VG-LLM work. Their complete main texts, tables, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original VG-LLM experiments on grounding, captioning, video object detection, spatial reasoning, and general multimodal benchmarks, including ablations and appendix results.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and reports additional 8B evaluations, fusion ablations, and training-data comparisons.

M1.justification: The selected method retains the VGGT geometry encoder, Qwen2.5-VL backbone, patch-level additive fusion, and next-token training objective. The larger backbone and alternative fusion experiments do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V3 introduces VLM-3R training data, alone and combined with the original SPAR-7M/LLaVA-Hound mixture, in Section 4.3.2. This extends training coverage within spatial reasoning. The dedicated BLINK spatial-subset breakdown disappears, but BLINK remains evaluated among the generic benchmarks.

E2.justification: V3 adds cross-attention and Concat+MLP comparison variants and includes Qwen2.5-VL-7B controls in detection and generic evaluations. V2's dedicated BLINK spatial comparison, including Claude-3-OPUS, CogVLM, and Yi-VL-34B, is removed. The principal ScanRefer, Scan2Cap, VSI-Bench, and CV-Bench comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: The stated batch size changes from 16 to 64, and experiments expand to 7B backbones and 8B total models. The earlier 3B-based spatial ablation is replaced by a larger-model study with original, VLM-3R, and combined training data. These substantially expand the experimental design; retained scene splits and IoU thresholds are unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds substantive tests of additive fusion against one- and three-layer cross-attention and concatenation, and replaces the small spatial ablation with comparisons across three training-data compositions. These test design choices and dependence on training data beyond v2's analyses. The appendix also removes one grounding failure example and one detection example.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance procedures. V3's explanation of relative-accuracy thresholds describes benchmark scoring, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V3 revises the 4B VSI-Bench average from 46.1 to 47.3 and CV-Bench average from 82.1 to 79.5, updates generic scores, and adds 8B and new ablation results. The 8B VSI-Bench average is 50.7. Existing 4B scene-understanding scores remain, despite reversed grounding-table parentheses. The revised training setup prevents interpreting the updated scores as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The token, feature-fusion, coordinate, and bounding-box formulations remain equivalent. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears. Additional explanations of existing evaluation metrics do not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The central contribution of incorporating video-derived geometry priors remains unchanged. V3's introduction adds an 8B state-of-the-art claim on VSI-Bench, and the conclusion no longer restricts its performance claim to the 4B model.

C2.justification: V3 emphasizes that dense captioning is conditioned on detected 3D proposals, qualifying v2's 'pure-vision' interpretation without changing the documented dependency. It adds interpretations of fusion and data-composition experiments. New Appendix E identifies possible performance overestimation from overlap between VGGT pretraining data and evaluation datasets such as ScanNet.

D1.justification: V3 documents alternative fusion implementations and matched baseline input settings. Reported 4B training times change from 10/12 hours to 9/7 hours for scene understanding/spatial reasoning, with 8B times added. It removes the appendix's conflicting 5e-6 learning-rate statement, retaining the main-text 1e-5 schedule. Hardware and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds the VLM-3R citation for its training-data analysis and removes references associated with the discarded BLINK discussion, including Depth in the Wild, Visual Spatial Reasoning, Wild6D, and Yi. Section 2's substantive positioning against prior 3D-aware MLLMs remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the experimental narrative. Training details move into Section 4, Section 4.3 becomes two analysis subsections, and acknowledgments and limitations/broader-impact appendices are added. The main section sequence and most introduction, related-work, and method exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Several result displays are substantially restructured: detection tables gain model-size groups, the generic-results table is transposed, and ablation tables are expanded or replaced. The appendix detection table becomes two tables with objects as rows. Grounding parentheses change meaning, the dedicated BLINK table is removed, and appendix image grids are shortened and rearranged.

improvement.justification: The added fusion and training-data controls better support key design choices, while clearer proposal dependence and pretraining-overlap limitations improve transparency. These gains are moderated by removal of the detailed BLINK comparison and new reporting inconsistencies: for example, the 8B six-frame bathtub F1 is 40.4 in Table 3 but 45.2 in Appendix Table 10. Overall, the stronger analysis and qualifications provide a limited net improvement.
